kaikki_vikisozluk.t:
Etymology tree
Proto-Semitic *šim
Proto-West Semitic *him
Arabic إن
Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *him, from Proto-Semitic *šim.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: إِنَّ • (ʔinna)
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Cognate to Hebrew הִנֵּה (“lo, behold”).
g: indeed, an emphasizing sentence particle, usually untranslated

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: إِنْ • (ʔin)
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Cognate to Hebrew אין (ein).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e:
إن (form I)
# إِنَّ (ʔinna) /ʔin.na/: inflection of آنَ (ʔāna):
## third-person feminine plural past active
## second-person feminine plural imperative
# إِنْ (ʔin) /ʔin/: second-person masculine singular imperative of آنَ (ʔāna)

إن (form I)
# إِنَّ (ʔinna) /ʔin.na/: second-person masculine singular imperative of أَنَّ (ʔanna)
# إِنِّ (ʔinni) /ʔin.ni/: second-person masculine singular imperative of أَنَّ (ʔanna)
أَنَّ • (ʔanna)
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Adverbial accusative of the noun underlying the former conjunction.
g: that (introduces an equational clause or a verb phrase)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e:
أن (form I)
# أُنَّ (ʔunna) /ʔun.na/: inflection of آنَ (ʔāna):
## third-person feminine plural past active
## second-person feminine plural imperative
# أُنْ (ʔun) /ʔun/: second-person masculine singular imperative of آنَ (ʔāna)
أَنَانِيّ • (ʔanāniyy) (feminine أَنَانِيَّة (ʔanāniyya), masculine plural أَنَانِيُّون (ʔanāniyyūn), feminine plural أَنَانِيَّات (ʔanāniyyāt))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Relative adjective (nisba) composed of أَنَا (ʾana, “I”) + ـَانـ (-ān-) + ـِيّ (-iyy).
s: Relative adjective (nisba) composed of أَنَا (ʾana, “I”) + ـَانـ (-ān-) + ـِيّ (-iyy)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَنَّى • (ʔannā)
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Compare Hausa ina (/⁠ínā⁠/, “where, how”).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَنَانِيَّة • (ʔanāniyya) f
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Relative noun (nisba) composed of أَنَانِيّ (ʔanāniyy, “egotistical”) + ـَة (-a).
s: Relative noun (nisba) composed of أَنَانِيّ (ʔanāniyy, “egotistical”) + ـَة (-a)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَنَانِيَّة • (ʔanāniyya)
أَنَّة • (ʔanna) f (plural أَنَّات (ʔannāt))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Morphologically from the root ء ن ن (ʔ n n).
g: a groan, moan, sigh, wail, whimper

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: إِنَاء • (ʔināʔ) m (plural آنِيَة (ʔāniya) or أَوَانٍ (ʔawānin, construct state أَوَانِي (ʔawānī)))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Derived from Proto-Semitic. Compare Hebrew אֳנִיָּה (ʾŏnīyá, “ship”), Aramaic מָאנָא / ܡܳܐܢܳܐ (mānā, “vessel, container; ship”), Ugaritic 𐎀𐎐𐎊𐎚 (ảnyt, “ship”), Akkadian 𒃻𒄘𒈾 (/⁠unūtu, anūtu⁠/, “household, palace; ship; utensils, instruments, tools, wares, gear”) – whence Jewish Babylonian Aramaic אנותא, אנתא (“a type of jar for oil, cruse”) and Old Armenian անօթ (anōtʻ, “container”) –, Ge'ez ንዋይ (nəway, “vessel, utensil, instrument, item; goods, possessions, property, wealth, estate”). It is generally assumed that there has been an accumulation of dissimilations in all these forms.
s: Akkadian 𒃻𒄘𒈾 (/⁠unūtu, anūtu⁠/, “household, palace; ship; utensils, instruments, tools, wares, gear”)
Ge'ez ንዋይ (nəway, “vessel, utensil, instrument, item; goods, possessions, property, wealth, estate”)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَوَان • (ʔawān) m (plural آوِنَة (ʔāwina))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed from Middle Persian [script needed] (ʾwʾm), [script needed] (ʾʾwʾm /⁠āwām⁠/, “space of time; epoch; occasion”), from Old Persian *abigāmā f (“time”), from 𐎠𐎲𐎡𐎹 (abi-, “towards”) + Proto-Indo-European *gem- (“to press, to grasp”). Also borrowed in إِبَّان (ʔibbān).
g: particular time, timeframe, occasion, time that has come or is due

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَنِيَ • (ʔaniya) I (non-past يَأْنَى (yaʔnā), verbal noun إِنًى (ʔinan))
أَنِيّ • (ʔaniyy) m
g: a thing of which the time has come, a thing which has attained maturity (for example a ripe plant)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: آوِنَة • (ʔāwina) m pl
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: آنَى • (ʔānā) IV (non-past يُؤْنِي (yuʔnī), verbal noun إِينَاء (ʔīnāʔ))
g: to postpone; to put off; to delay; to defer; to retard
to restrain; to withold; to impede

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَنَاءَ • (ʔanāʔa) IV (non-past يُنِيءُ (yunīʔu), verbal noun إِنَاءَة (ʔināʔa))
إِنِّيَّة • (ʔinniyya) f (plural إِنِّيَّات (ʔinniyyāt))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From إِنِّي (ʔinnī, “Indeed, I am”), composed of إِنَّ (ʔinna, an emphasizing sentence particle) + ـنِي (-nī, “me”). Also often hypothesized to be from Ancient Greek εἶναι (eînai, “be, exist”).
s: إِنَّ (ʔinna, an emphasizing sentence particle) + ـنِي (-nī, “me”)
